text: trying to focus but not finding purchase, chest heaving. As tempting as it was to tease him over his insanely stupid hiding spot, Jake held it back. Now was not the time. Not when Gabriel wouldn’t make eye contact. Not when he saw the dried blood along his knuckles or the way his hands wouldn’t uncurl. “Shit. Shitshitshit — hang on, man.” Jake moved fast, on his knees beside the pod in seconds, hands working at the seam. "Okay — okay, it’s stuck. Hang on. I’ve got you." His callused hands ripped at the seams, searching for a latch, anything. There was nothing but warped metal and rusted lock housings, sealed like a coffin. Gabriel’s fingers dragged against the glass again, slower this time. Jake’s pulse spiked. “Not on my watch.” He sprinted to a collapsed wall of the ship, pulling a scrap of bent piping free from the wreckage, jamming it into the seam and wrenching hard. It took him two tries to wedge it in properly, another four to torque the metal enough to squeal . The rust shrieked. The whole pod shuddered. Inside, Gabriel’s breath hitched, his head knocking faintly against the padding as he tried to stay conscious. “Stay with me, Gabs. Keep breathing. I’ve got you.” One more wrench and the seam tore, glass spider-webbing with a crack that roared too loud in the empty wreckage. Jake shoved until the lock gave way, the door slamming open with a gust of stale, burning air. Jake hauled Gabriel up and over the edge of the pod by the front of his shirt. He poured out, boneless against Jake as he was pulled clear; coughs tearing up through starved lungs, fingers clawing instinctively at Jake’s shirt as if still trying to climb away from the pod. “Easy, easy. You’re out.” Jake pressed a hand to the back of Gabriel’s neck, grounding him, steadying the tremble in his limbs. “She ain’t got you. You’re okay.” They stayed like that for a while, hunched beside the cracked pod while the Fog curled low and heavy around them. Jake ran slow circles across Gabriel’s back, waiting as the adrenaline bled out of starved muscles. Gabriel’s shoulders shook — not from panic anymore, but the ghost of it, nerves burning off in a soft, rattled laugh. “Holy shit...That was — way too close.” Jake let out a breath he hadn’t realized he’d been holding. “No kidding. This — this is exactly why we don’t improvise, you absolute dumbass .” Gabriel stirred, one arm twitching upward, fingers fumbling through his jacket pocket. He pulled out a worn keycard and held it up with the slow, lazy pride of a man who just barely won a bet with death. “Thought you might like a new toolkit,” he croaked. Jake stared at the card, then back at him. At the bruised knuckles, the glassy eyes, the total lack of sense that somehow still walked around in a human body. “You’re a fucking idiot,” he muttered, but took the card anyway. Gabriel laughed — wheezy, spent, but defiant. Jake huffed out a reluctant chuckle of his own, scrubbing a hand down his face. “Don’t ever scare me like that again.” “No promises.” Behind them, the pod door hung open like a wound, fog curling out from its seams like smoke from a grave. Somewhere distant, the Huntress’s lullaby drifted through the wreckage — soft, echoing, and much too close.
